spec.title: Chrony - Time Offset  - Root Delay - Root Dispersion
spec.description:
time_offset:
The time offset between the system clock and the NTP server.

root_delay :
The total network delay to the NTP server, including all intermediate hops.

root_dispersion :
The total dispersion or uncertainty of the time from the reference clock.

spec.title: Chrony - clock_last_measure & clock_last_update
spec.description:
clock_last_meas:
The timestamp of the last measurement received from the NTP server.
Chrony Tracking Log Equivalent: This corresponds to the time of the last update (not directly shown in chronyc tracking but can be seen with chronyc sources).

clock_last_update (Collectd):
The time of the last clock update.
Chrony Tracking Log Equivalent: This indicates when the last update to the system clock occurred, matching the Date and Time fields in the tracking log.

spec.title: Chrony - Skew PPM & Frequency Error
spec.description:
Skew ppm (Skew in parts per million)
The estimated error (or "skew") in the frequency offset measurement, in parts per million.
A lower value means the frequency offset is well-known and stable.
Example: 0.100 ppm, meaning the error in the frequency measurement is quite small.

frequency_error:
Represents the frequency error in parts per million (ppm), showing the difference between the system clock and the reference clock.
Chrony Tracking Log Equivalent: Matches the Freq ppm (Frequency offset) field in the tracking log.

spec.title: Chrony - clock_mode & clock_reachability
spec.description:
clock_mode represents the operational mode of the NTP server with respect to synchronization.

A value of 0 generally means that the server is in normal operating mode and is actively synchronizing time.

--
clock_reachability is an 8-bit octal value that tracks whether the NTP client has been able to reach the server over the last eight polling intervals.

A value of 255 (which is 11111111 in binary) means that the NTP client has successfully reached the server in all of the last 8 polling intervals.
Each bit represents a successful or failed communication attempt with the NTP server:

All bits set to 1 (i.e., 255) indicates that all communication attempts in the recent past were successful.
Lower values (e.g., 128, which is 10000000 in binary) indicate fewer successful attempts, meaning the client may have had difficulty reaching the server in some polling intervals.
